```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B has sourced evidence that people pay for this as a standalone product. Prerender.io's published pricing lists tiers at $49, $149 and $349/mo, and its pricing page carries a named customer testimonial. A's only sourced evidence of willingness to pay is for the feature bundled inside full MFT platforms (Files.com at $199-499/mo, Nodinite on an annual license). A's own Open Question #1 says it is unknown whether anyone will pay for it standalone.",
    "B's demand signals are recent (Reddit threads from 2022 to 2025) and directly describe the problem the product solves. A's quotes date from 2012 and 2016, and one of them describes a different problem.",
    "A's Case Against undercuts its own buyer segment. A competitor's copy says the tool can be built 'with a cron job and a Slack webhook in an afternoon', the forum threads show users doing exactly that, and Files.com already bundles the capability. That leaves a narrow group of teams who are too busy to script it yet would pay for it.",
    "For a 90-day horizon, B's main structural risk matters less. That risk is Google downgrading dynamic rendering to a workaround in favor of SSR/SSG, which is a long-term shrinkage. A's main risk, that the product is a feature rather than a business, would block the first sale itself.",
    "B's buyers gather in identifiable free communities (r/TechSEO, r/reactjs, r/angular) where they ask for this fix unprompted. That gives a solo operator a zero-cash route to early prospects, although the brief does not source its cost or conversion. A's sourced paid-search channel costs $3-8+ per click against incumbents that already rank for the relevant queries."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence is the weakest part of its brief. The 2012 StackOverflow quote ('someone can't log in to upload the files') is about SFTP server availability, not about missing or late file arrival. That is the problem WatchFor solves, and the brief says WatchFor is not a match for this idea. The HN 'seed quote' is a bare link with no quoted content. The only on-target quote is a single 2016 education-forum post. Together these are thin and dated support for current, paying demand for file-arrival monitoring.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. B has significant gaps of its own. Its Reddit quotes have no URLs. It cites seven competitors but does not include the list in the brief. The claim that thin competitors 'run profitably' is unsourced. Its sourced SEO CAC of $480-942 assumes a 7-month payback, which is too slow for a 90-day goal. Saturation and low switching costs may also make the first sale hard to win. B wins mainly because a standalone paid market is evidenced and A's is not, not because B's own evidence is strong."
}
```
